title: Usage Spend Runway Playbook
summary: A lightweight worksheet + playbook to compute customer billing runway, recommend alert thresholds for token spend and rate limits, and provide canned actions / Slack templates for QBRs and renewal conversations.
body:
Purpose:
This is a practical worksheet for CS managers and AE partners to quickly estimate a customer's spend runway, identify imminent billing or rate-limit risks, and surface prescriptive next steps for QBRs and renewal conversations. It focuses on token-based billing profiles (hosted API usage), burst rate limits, and how to convert usage telemetry into clear action items.

When to use:
- Pre-QBR: run this worksheet 7 days before the QBR to flag risks and propose mitigation.
- Renewal risk check: run monthly for accounts near contract threshold or with high month-over-month growth.
- Alert tuning: use to propose new alert thresholds for customer accounts.

Key inputs (fill from billing + telemetry):
- Customer name: {{customer_name}}
- Billing period / invoice cycle: e.g., monthly
- Committed spend (if any): $ / month
- Total remaining budget for current cycle: $remaining_budget
- Current plan token price (per 1K tokens): $token_price_per_1k
- Avg daily token consumption (30d): avg_daily_tokens
- 7-day peak day tokens: peak_7d_tokens
- 1h peak RPS recorded: peak_rps
- Current rate limit tier: e.g., 200 rps / 50K tokens/min
- Cache hit ratio (if using Redwood caching): cache_hit_pct

Quick calculations (manual formulas):
- Avg daily $ spend = (avg_daily_tokens / 1000) * token_price_per_1k
- Projected days until budget depletion = remaining_budget / Avg daily $ spend
- Spike factor = peak_7d_tokens / avg_daily_tokens   (use to understand burst risk)
- Effective tokens served after cache = avg_daily_tokens * (1 - cache_hit_pct)

Runway bands (recommendation, adjustable):
- Green: projected_days >= 30 -> low urgency
- Yellow: 7 <= projected_days < 30 -> actionable; trigger AE/CS sync and quota review
- Red: projected_days < 7 -> escalate to solutions engineering + propose temporary quota bump or discount conversion

Alert thresholds to propose (examples):
- Daily spend alert: 50% of monthly committed budget used within first 14 days -> WARNING
- Daily spikes: day-to-day increase > 2x avg_daily_tokens -> AUTO INVESTIGATE
- Rate limit breach frequency: >3 rate limit errors/day over last 3 days -> ESCALATE
- Sustained RPS > 80% of rate limit over 30m -> PROACTIVE SCALE DISCUSSION

Channels & escalation matrix (suggested):
- 1) CS owner Slack DM + account AE: immediate notification for Yellow/Red
- 2) Create internal ticket in CS queue (CS-XXXX) with tags: billing-risk, runway, urgent
- 3) If Red: schedule 30-minute triage with Solutions Eng + Infra to evaluate short-term dedicated capacity or temporary quota increase

Canned Slack/Email templates (short):
- Slack (early warning): "Heads-up: {{customer_name}}'s projected runway for this billing cycle is {{projected_days}} days (Avg daily spend ${{avg_daily_spend}}). Recommend we review cached endpoints and potential throttles before the QBR. Can AE pull usage patterns for top 5 APIs?"
- Email to AE/CS lead (escalation): "Subject: ACTION: {{customer_name}} Billing Runway <7 days - immediate review needed
Hi team,
We flagged a high burn rate for {{customer_name}} (projected runway: {{projected_days}} days). Attached: quick chart of 7d/30d token trends and rate limit events. Recommend: 1) Temporary quota increase 2) Prioritized engineering review on endpoint caching 3) Customer call to discuss commit or throttling.
Thanks,
CS Ops"

QBR slide checklist (what to bring):
- One-slide snapshot: spend this cycle vs commitment, projected runway, top 3 drivers of spend
- Token waterfall: calls by route (top 10 endpoints) and whether they are cacheable
- Rate-limit incidents: count and impact last 30 days
- Action plan and ask (commit increase? quota bump? revised retry/backoff?)
- Success metrics post-action (reduced tokens/day, fewer rate-limit incidents)

Investigations & data pulls (practical queries to run):
- Pull top 50 endpoints by tokens consumed over last 7 days (include user IDs if privacy allows)
- Timeseries of tokens/day with 1h granularity for last 14 days to identify burst patterns
- List of 429/5xx errors and mapping to SDK versions or specific API routes

Playbook decision table (simple):
- If spike factor > 3 AND projected_days < 14 -> open Red path: immediate triage + propose temporary quota + customer call
- If cacheable_ratio > 40% and spend high -> propose caching configuration changes + dev doc + follow up in 2 weeks
- If repeated rate-limit hits but low overall spend -> optimize retry/backoff guidance and reduce client concurrency

Suggested artifacts to attach to QBR doc:
- 7d/30d token trend chart (png)
- Top endpoints table (csv)
- Rate limit incident log (sheet)

Notes to CS reps (handy heuristics):
- Customers often misinterpret burst events from batch data pipelines as normal app traffic; check for ETL job windows.
- Recommend default alert cadence: daily digest for Green, immediate DM for Yellow/Red.
- When in doubt, propose a short-term 30-day commit to stabilize spend and buy time for longer-term optimizations.

Action tracker template (to copy into ticket body):
- Action: (e.g., request quota bump)
- Owner: (name)
- Due: (date)
- Status: open/in_progress/complete
- Notes: free-text

Open questions / TODOs for this doc (for CS Ops):
- Add calculated sample sheet with live fields tied to billing export for customers on commits.
- Build a one-click Slack alert creation flow in CS tooling that seeds messages above.
- Map common SDK versions that trigger known burst patterns and publish guidance for customers.

End of document.

(Working draft - intended to be lightweight and actionable. Use and modify during pre-QBR runs.)
